## Reproducibility and the file {#reproducibility-and-the-file}

:::: {.none}
::: {.fragment}
The class got $\chi^2$ = `r fmt_num(an("5X3KG", "statistic_recorded"), 3)`, to the third decimal. That is reproducibility, and it is the easy R.
:::

::: {.fragment}
It shows that **the code and the file** give the number on record. It does not show that the file measures what the paper measured, and here it did not.
:::

::: {.fragment}
The check that finds such an error comes **before any model**: count the cases and their outcomes, and set them beside the published description of the sample.
:::
::::

::: notes
Step back and look at what just happened. The whole class, on different machines, one number, agreeing to the third decimal. That is reproducibility, and notice how cheap it was: you all ran the same code on the same file, so of course you got the same number. [advance] And yet the number points the wrong way. A reproduction tells you that the computation was faithful to its inputs; it is silent about the inputs. The file was built by careful people, with a rule that is right for most unions, and its error shows only in the counts. [advance] So the check belongs at the start, not the end: before any model, count the cases and how they ended, and hold them up against what the paper says its sample was. One analyst of five did that, and it took a few minutes.
:::
